This only controls the output resolution of the DisplayLink chip in the adapter. For USB-C DisplayPort connections, the resolution is determined by Android automatically.
Create the virtual display as a trusted display. This enables other apps to set keyboard policy and other features. Requires Shizuku.

Flags used to create the trusted virtual display. Picks the recommended set for this Android version by default. Changes apply the next time a display is created. Combinations rejected by the system fall back to automatic; see Logs for details.
Apps can open windows on the display and the system may mirror the contents of other displays onto it. Unset creates a private display.
Register as a presentation display. Apps may automatically project their content to it for second-screen experiences.
Mark the display secure. Creation requires the CAPTURE_SECURE_VIDEO_OUTPUT permission, which is reserved for system components.
Allow content to be displayed while the keyguard is shown but insecure. Private displays only; mutually exclusive with PUBLIC.
The display can be associated with a touchpad device that matches its unique ID.
Destroy contents once the display is removed. Public displays without this flag move their content to the main display stack.
Support and always show system decorations: home, navigation bar and wallpaper. Does not work without TRUSTED.
Trust the display to show system decorations and receive inputs without the user\'s touch.
Place the display in a new display group instead of the default display group.
Keep the display unlocked with no keyguard on it. Only valid for displays that are not in the default display group.
Do not play sound effects or perform haptic feedback when the user touches the screen.
Maintain own focus and touch mode. The display must be trusted to have its own focus.
Place the display in a display group associated with its virtual device instead of the default display group.
Do not become the top focused display by stealing top focus from another display. Ignored without OWN_FOCUS.
Always mirror the built-in screen to the external display using MediaProjection. Launching apps onto the display will not be possible.

Simple advice for connecting and getting the most from AirLink.
Connect your phone and TV to the same Wi-Fi. Open AirPlay on the TV, scan for receivers, choose one and approve screen capture. Protected video might not mirror.
Start Sunshine from the Moonlight screen, then pair a Moonlight client. Extra remote input features may require Shizuku.
Use a compatible DisplayLink USB adapter and follow its driver setup. This requires supported hardware.
Check both devices are on the same network, enable AirPlay, disable VPN or guest network isolation and scan again. Manual IP is under Mirror to TV.
Allow audio capture when requested. Some apps block audio capture. If too quiet, try switching off Follow phone media volume in Mirror to TV settings.
AirLink does not intentionally reset the TV volume on connection. Use the TV remote for speaker volume. If it still changes, disconnect and share your TV software version.
Android asks for screen capture when connecting. Floating controls and Shizuku are optional. Audio capture requires permission.
